sources: dossier=Superseded/historical: 'Lifecycle events all fire from control-api (pre-2026-05-24 invariant) -> relaxed: events fire from the process owning the state transition's post-commit fan-out (control-api for template/instance events; supervisor for sub-graph/fan-out run-scope terminals) (2026-05-24 artifact)', corroborated by the RESOLVED 2026-07-14 transcript-tier teardown ruling naming OnRunScopeTerminal/OnInstanceTerminated as distinct firings; doc=control-api.md:26 said 'fire from control-api (not the supervisor)' and Boundaries:21 claimed sole ownership of 'the lifecycle-subscriber fan-out'; code=lifecycle_fanout.go:17 FanOutRunScopeEvent called from child_execution.go:216,362 (supervisor runtime), config/supervisor.go:106 DialLifecycleSubscribers
note: control-api.md flatly contradicted its own neighbor concept doc lifecycle-subscriber.md (two-firer model), the dossier's 2026-05-24 relaxation, and code. Rewrote the invariant and Boundaries line to name both firers by event category.

sources: dossier=2026-07-06 transcript: graceful terminate 'lets the current frame finish, then rejects new messages, opens no new frames' (the transition is not instantaneous with the request); design corpus=lifecycle-subscriber.md:25 says 'a slow subscriber holds up the firing process's path' (not 'the response'); code=instances.go:384,567 call FanOutInstanceEvent synchronously in-request for other transitions, but the kill/terminate handler (instances.go:705-755, MarkTerminated) has no such call -- OnInstanceTerminated is delivered later by instance_terminator.go tick (line 130), a 2s poll
note: The doc's 'a slow subscriber holds up the response' framing is imprecise for graceful termination: per the dossier's own transcript-tier graceful-teardown model the instance-terminated transition hasn't happened yet when the terminate request returns, so nothing can hold up that response by definition -- the poll-based delivery is a correct implementation of firing synchronously with the actual transition, just not with the triggering request. Reworded to match lifecycle-subscriber.md's more precise 'firing process's path' language and called out the termination case explicitly.

sources: dossier=Breakpoints/debugger section: 'Breakpoint hits are discoverable by polling: MCP resources/read over two URI families with a request-carried ?since= cursor (no server session state)' (2026-05-24/28, artifacts) -- confirms the resource surface is intentional and separate from the tool catalog; doc=control-api.md invariant (old line 29) described only the tool-invocation re-entry path, silent on resources; code=mcp_route.go:43-46 wires Resources: newBreakpointResourceCatalog alongside the registry-derived Tools catalog; mcp_resources.go queries persistence directly under mcp:read + in-handler breakpoint:read, no router re-entry
note: The dossier corroborates the MCP resource surface exists by design; the doc simply omitted it from the auth-gate invariant, which would mislead a reader auditing the auth story. Added a sentence naming the resource surface and its distinct (non-router-re-entry) auth path.

sources: dossier=Net position: 'All HTTP routes live under a /v1/ prefix, including the executor async-callback URL and the observability sub-router; old bare paths were removed with no transition window (2026-06-08, corpus-bootstrap, artifact)'; doc=control-api.md:25 said 'unversioned at the wire'; code=app.go:76 r.Route("/v1", ...), actions.go BuildV1Registry with literal /v1/ prefixes
note: Dossier directly contradicts the doc's literal claim -- the wire does carry a version token. The doc's intended meaning (no negotiation, single live version) is real design intent per the dossier, so reworded to say that precisely instead of 'unversioned'.

sources: dossier=Net position: 'The compose: reserved prefix on tags/instance-keys is server-enforced... (2026-06-06, comprehensive-gap-closure, artifact)'; design corpus=concepts/rimsky.md defines the 'Compose surface -- manifest-driven project orchestration' under concept:rimsky; concepts.md catalog has no standalone compose slug; doc=control-api.md invariant used the bare term 'compose' with no resolving citation
note: The compose machinery is real and dossier-confirmed, but the term was undefined within the design corpus's self-containment rules (a fresh reader could misread it as Docker Compose). Fixed by naming it as the CLI's compose surface and citing concept:rimsky, which does define it.
